project_type: Node.js Express server serving static HTML/CSS/JS frontend (single-page app pattern in index.html)
build_system: npm - no build step, just 'npm install' for express dependency
test_framework: None - no tests in the project
test_command: node -e "require('./server.js')" (basic syntax check - no test suite exists)
verification_instructions: 1. Run 'npm install' to install dependencies. 2. Start server with 'node server.js' and verify it starts without errors. 3. Verify /scanner.html is served as a static file. 4. Verify the new API endpoint for scanned document upload responds correctly.
environment_constraints: Open network - can install npm packages. No build tools needed. App uses only Express as a dependency. Frontend is plain HTML/CSS/JS with no framework or bundler. PDF generation must happen client-side in the browser (using jsPDF from CDN or bundled). Image processing (contrast, sharpening) must happen client-side using Canvas API.
contribution_requirements: No formal contributing guide. Keep the same patterns: static HTML files in /public/, API routes in server.js, file storage in /uploads/, state in state.json.
key_patterns: 1. Each page is a separate .html file in /public/ (index.html, agreement.html, receipt.html). 2. Server has custom multipart parser (no multer). 3. Upload endpoints save files as 'type-{customerId}.pdf' in /uploads/. 4. Customer state stored in state.json as flat JSON. 5. CSS is inline in each HTML file. 6. No external CDN for existing pages - but scanner page will need jsPDF. 7. UI uses purple/navy color scheme with CSS custom properties. 8. Mobile-friendly meta viewport already set.
directory_structure: Root: server.js (Express app), package.json, state.json (data). /public/: static HTML pages (index.html, agreement.html, receipt.html, logo.jpg). /uploads/: stored PDF files.
